question: Which meristematic tissue has the highest levels of Auxin?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Apical Meristematic Tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apical Meristematic Tissue** is located at the tips of roots and shoots and is responsible for primary growth in plants.
 
• It has the **highest levels of Auxin**, a plant hormone that promotes cell elongation and differentiation, especially in young plant tissues.
 
• Auxin concentration is critical in **cell division and elongation**, facilitating the vertical growth of roots and shoots.
 
• The apical meristem is also involved in the formation of primary tissues such as the epidermis, cortex, and vascular tissues.
 
• Due to its active growth role, the apical meristem has a higher metabolic activity compared to other meristematic tissues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lateral Meristematic Tissue:**

 
 
• Located along the sides of stems and roots, responsible for secondary growth (increasing girth).
 
• Examples include the vascular cambium and cork cambium.
 
• Auxin levels are comparatively lower here than in apical meristem.
 
 
 
• **Intercalary Meristematic Tissue:**
 
 
• Found at the base of leaves or internodes, especially in monocots like grasses.
 
• Promotes regrowth in damaged grass and contributes to elongation of internodes.
 
• Auxin levels are moderate compared to apical meristem.
 
 
 
• **Xylem:**
 
 
• Xylem is a permanent tissue responsible for water and nutrient transport within plants.
 
• It does not produce Auxin as it is not a meristematic tissue.
 
• It forms part of the vascular system and includes tracheids and vessel elements.
 
 
 
• **Auxin:**
 
 
• A plant hormone discovered by F.W. Went, essential for growth and development.
 
• Functions include cell elongation, apical dominance, and root formation.
 
• Transported from the apical meristem downwards through the plant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Apical dominance:**

 
 
• Auxin produced in the apical meristem suppresses lateral bud growth, ensuring vertical growth.
 
• Removal of the apical meristem can lead to bushy growth due to activation of lateral buds.
 
 
 
• **
 
 
• Auxin is transported via polar transport (cell-to-cell movement) and vascular tissues.
 
• This transport plays a significant role in plant tropisms, such as phototropism and gravitropism.
 
 
 
• Applications of Auxin:**
 
 
• Used in agriculture for rooting cuttings and promoting growth in tissue culture.
 
• Synthetic auxins, such as 2,4-D, are used as herbicides to control weeds.
